sections.h2: Who to call about Livingston County property tax
sections.html:
Three offices share the work, all in or near the courthouse square in Smithland. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) sets the value of each parcel. The sheriff sends and collects the bill. The county clerk takes over once a bill is certified as delinquent. Knowing which office owns which question saves you a few wasted calls.

Livingston County offices
OfficeCall aboutPhoneAddress and hours
Property Valuation AdministratorValue disputes, exemptions, ownership records270-928-2524PO Box 77, Smithland, KY 42081
SheriffAmount owed, payoff figures, payment270-928-2122321 Court Street (PO Box 340); weekdays 8 to 4
County ClerkRecorded liens, delinquent bills, tax sales270-928-2162321 Court Street (PO Box 400); Monday 8 to 5, Tuesday through Friday 8 to 4

The sheriff also handles court security and civil papers, so the tax counter is one of several things happening at that desk.

Livingston is a small rural county with settled households, and it belongs to the Paducah metro area. The middle owner-occupied home is worth $125,600, and owners live in 81.2 percent of the homes. Median gross rent is $926. Few people move in a given year, since 93.8 percent stayed at the same address, and one resident in four (25.1 percent) is 65 or older.

Population was 8,888 in the 2020 census, and the July 2025 estimate of 8,863 is almost flat. Few listings come up, and buyers often come from nearby Paducah. The community of Ledbetter sits across the Tennessee River from that city and is the largest place in the county. If you own farmland or river acreage, expect the buyer pool to be smaller and more local than for a house in town.

sections.h2: When the tax bill is due
sections.html:
Kentucky gives owners until December 31 of the assessment year to pay. Paying early earns a discount: 2 percent off for a full payment made by November 1. The next two months carry the plain amount, January adds 5 percent, and 10 percent applies after that. If the state approves a late schedule for a county, each stage lasts about a month instead.

The sheriff turns over what remains unpaid on April 15. The clerk then records the lien, and the debt picks up 1 percent interest each month. The state's walk-through of a $1,000 bill shows $1,254 at the handoff, $1,627.61 if paid in May after a second month of interest, and $1,704.21 for a buyer at the clerk's sale. That last figure becomes the base on which the buyer later charges interest and fees.

Before any sale the clerk must run the delinquent list in a newspaper and on a county-sponsored site. The county attorney also mails a 30-day warning to each owner, with a second warning if needed. Ask the Livingston County Clerk for the date of the current sale and the list of bills certified as delinquent.

sections.h2: How the PVA sets a value
sections.html:
Kentucky recognizes three main methods. For homes the PVA leans on the sales comparison approach, adjusting nearby sales up or down for differences such as a basement. Barns, fences and commercial buildings are valued at replacement cost minus depreciation. Rental properties are valued by the income they produce. Every parcel gets a physical look from the PVA's staff at least every four years.

Farmland is different. Under Section 172A of the Kentucky Constitution, it is assessed at agricultural value, not market value. The state's own example taxes an acre that would sell for $50,000 on an agricultural value of $750. The Revenue Department builds per-acre values for cropland, pasture, woodland and waste ground. Ask the PVA whether your parcel is classed as farm use before you assume a market-based figure.

Federal, state, county and city property is exempt, as are schools run by nonprofits and the buildings and personal property of religious institutions. A nonprofit or religious group applies on Revenue Form 62A023 through the PVA, and a denial can go to the local board.

Talk to the PVA first, and do it before the inspection period ends. Public viewing of the roll starts the first Monday of May and lasts thirteen days. After your conference, the clerk needs the paperwork by the end of the next workday. The board then sits at the county seat, Smithland, 25 to 35 days later.

Evidence wins or loses these cases. The board considers only what is presented while both sides are in the room, and it denies an appeal that arrives without documents. Photographs of the building, its construction cost, insurance policies, nearby listings and sales all help. A paid representative must hold one of the credentials Kentucky lists, such as attorney, accountant, broker or appraiser, and present your written authorization.

If the board changes a value, it must explain why in writing. A value that rises after bills have printed produces a supplemental bill.

Seniors can cut their bill. For assessment years 2025 and 2026 the homestead exemption removes $49,100 from the assessed value of the owner's home. Apply through the PVA and bring a license, birth certificate or passport that proves your age. A buyer cannot inherit the exemption and must file separately, so a sale ends it for you. If you are 65 or older and planning to sell, ask the PVA how the exemption will be handled for the year of the sale so the closing figures are not a surprise.

The year's bill belongs to whoever held title when January 1 arrived, and the closing statement divides the cost between buyer and seller. The seller also owes Kentucky's transfer tax under KRS 142.050, $0.50 on each $500 of price, collected as the deed is filed in Smithland. Foreclosure transfers and transfers between divorcing spouses are among the exemptions.

A delinquent amount stays attached to the property as a lien for up to eleven years, so expect the title agent to want it paid first. Before listing, get a payoff from the sheriff or, if the bill has been certified, from the clerk. A cash sale skips the wait for a buyer's lender to order title work, but the lien still has to be cleared from the proceeds at closing.

Bring the deed, your most recent tax bill and a photo ID when you visit the sheriff or clerk. Ask for the payoff in writing and for the good-through date, since interest accrues every month the debt stays open. Hand that figure to the title agent so it can be deducted at the closing table.

faqs.q: Where is the Livingston County sheriff's tax office?
faqs.a: It is at 321 Court Street in Smithland; mail goes to PO Box 340. Call 270-928-2122 on a weekday between 8 and 4.

faqs.q: What phone number reaches the Livingston County PVA?
faqs.a: Call 270-928-2524. The mailing address is PO Box 77, Smithland, KY 42081, and the office handles values, exemptions and ownership records.

faqs.q: Does Livingston County give a discount for paying early?
faqs.a: Yes. Pay the full bill by November 1 and it drops by 2 percent. After that you owe the printed amount until year end, and then penalties begin.

faqs.q: What happens to a Livingston County tax bill I never pay?
faqs.a: The sheriff sends it to the clerk after April 15, and a lien goes on record with interest and commissions piling up. Investors may buy the debt at a sale a few months later.

faqs.q: Is farmland taxed differently in Livingston County?
faqs.a: Yes. Kentucky assesses farmland at agricultural value rather than market value, using per-acre figures for cropland, pasture and woodland. Ask the PVA whether your acreage qualifies as farm use.
